correctness.rationale: Single cyclic 11 reflection forces every crossing palindrome to be centered on the join. Palindromicity realizes every such even-length factor, all distinct from linear. A three-family constructive Cantor induction supplies exactly 2n new linear palindromes when length n grows to 3n; universal palindrome bound gives exhaustiveness. Full ranges and boundary ranks stated; independent brute-force finite checks through rank five supplement the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Natural exact language-level invariant of circular strings: the cyclic-only palindromes are completely classified for a broad boundary-isolated palindrome class, with one per even length and zero per odd length. Application yields full-length Cantor spectrum and exact (N-1)/2 circular correction across all ranks. This distinguishes circular palindromic complexity from the previously studied linear spectrum and supplies a constructive benchmark for circular-factor algorithms.
